model_output:
Hello and welcome to our podcast episode on the founding of Instagram. Instagram is one of the most popular social media platforms in the world, with over 1 billion active users. But how did this revolutionary app get its start?

The idea for Instagram was born in 2010, when its co-founders, Kevin Systrom and Mike Krieger, were attending Stanford University. They saw a gap in the market for a mobile app that made it easy to share photos and videos with friends and family. They began working on the app in secret, using their own savings to fund its development.

In 2011, Instagram was launched on the App Store. It quickly gained popularity, thanks to its sleek interface and innovative features, such as filters and the ability to share photos on other social media platforms. In just over a year, the app had 1 million active users.

In 2012, Instagram was acquired by Facebook for $1 billion in cash and stock. This was a turning point for the company, as it gave them access to Facebook's vast resources and user base. Under Facebook's ownership, Instagram has continued to grow and evolve, adding new features such as Stories and Reels, and expanding into new markets around the world.

Despite some bumps in the road, including the departure of its co-founders and a data scandal, Instagram has remained a dominant force in the world of social media. Its impact on culture, commerce, and communication cannot be overstated.

In conclusion, the founding of Instagram was a brilliant idea that filled a gap in the market and changed the way people share and connect with each other. Its success is a testament to the hard work and ingenuity of its co-founders, and its impact on the world will be felt for years to come.
